title: Operator shadow simulator and incident communication templates
author: Priya Desai
summary: A practical program and set of templates to accelerate new responders from shadow to independent operator using synthetic stress simulations, a measurable progression matrix, and customer-facing status templates tailored to model-inference incidents.
body:
Overview

This page defines the Operator Shadow Simulator (OSS) program: a lightweight, repeatable set of synthetic incident exercises, paired with a structured shadow-to-solo progression, and standard customer/stakeholder communication templates. The OSS purpose is to:

- Verify operator proficiency on common Redwood serving incidents (throttling, KV-cache churn, multi-model fallbacks, and model-quality regressions).
- Provide a painless cadence for shadowing, knowledge transfer, and graded solo signoff.
- Ensure consistent, brand-safe external communications and status page updates during incidents.

Scope

Applicable to: oncall responders across SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, and Customer Success who will act as first- or second-line operators. Not intended for product design or long-format postmortems (separate process).

Program components

1) Synthetic stress scenarios (OSS scenarios)
   - KV-cache cold-start spike: simulate high prefix miss rates across multiple tenants.
   - Throttle/backpressure burst: backend GPU pool saturates causing 429/503 surface area.
   - Model-variant fallback cascade: primary model unavailable, fallback to quantized variant with longer latency.
   - Quality regression smoke test: controlled prompt set returns measurable quality drop (BLEU/ROUGE-style metric simulated).

Each scenario includes: objective, preconditions, injected signals, verifier checks, and expected operator actions.

2) Shadow-to-solo progression matrix (Operator progression)
   - Stage 0 — Orientation (0–2 days): read key runbooks, walk through runbook playflows, observe two live incidents.
   - Stage 1 — Guided shadow (1–2 weeks): shadowing shifts with checklist signoffs; complete OSS scenario A and B under guidance.
   - Stage 2 — Supervised practice (1 week): lead two OSS exercises with a mentor watching; fill evidence form.
   - Stage 3 — Solo signoff (pass criteria): independent response to a synthetic exercise and one low-impact live incident under review.

Progression criteria (pass/fail signals):
- Timely acknowledgment (under 2 minutes).
- Accurate severity classification and correct paging path.
- Correct containment action (e.g., capacity isolation, traffic shaping, rollback or model swap).
- Clean evidence chain (logs, traces, alert IDs) submitted within 30 minutes of stabilization.

Roles & responsibilities

- New responder: complete OSS orientation materials and schedule shadow shifts.
- Mentor (experienced operator): run through scenarios, provide real-time feedback, sign off evidence form.
- Rotation lead (oncall manager): approve solo signoff and update rota.
- Incident commander (IC): owns escalation during live incidents and coordinates customer comms.

OSS scenario example: KV-cache cold-start spike

Objective: Verify operator can identify cache-miss driven latency spike and perform a controlled cache-warmup + autoscaler adjustment without causing broad restarts.

Preconditions: Synthetic traffic generator enabled against staging pool; monitoring dashboards show 95th percentile latency rising; cache hit ratio drops below 60%.

Injected signals:
1. Spike in 'kv_cache_miss_rate' for tenant T01 to 75% for 10 minutes.
2. Increased 'inflight_requests_per_gpu' metric crossing 90% threshold.

Verifier checks (pass criteria):
- Operator escalates to SLO-tier 2 within 10 minutes.
- Performs controlled cache-warmup script (oss/cache-warmup.sh) without restarting serving processes.
- Confirms 95th percentile latency reduces by at least 30% within 15 minutes.

Playbook steps (step-by-step):
1. Acknowledge page and join bridge.
2. Run 'k8s get pods' and locate impacted node(s).
3. Check dashboards: kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_miss_rate, inflight_requests_per_gpu.
4. Run cache-warmup script:

   # Example cache warmup command (staging)
   ./oss/scripts/cache-warmup.sh --tenant T01 --model redwood-base-1 --duration 300

5. If warmup has no effect after 10 minutes, scale up pool by +1 instance (follow autoscale SOP).
6. Document all commands and timestamps to evidence form.

Automation hooks

- The OSS harness posts a synthetic incident ticket to the responder Slack channel and triggers the oncall pager for realistic timing.
- Each run auto-creates a case in JIRA with prefilled template for evidence capture.

Operator resilience scorecard (post-exercise)

- Acknowledge time: 0–2 min — green; 2–5 min — yellow; >5 min — red.
- Containment correctness: pass/fail with notes.
- Evidence completeness: % of required fields completed.
- Communication clarity: mentor-rated 1–5.

Simulation logistics and cadence

- Monthly OSS run for each oncall rotation block (default: first week of rotation).
- Ad-hoc OSS runs may be scheduled by rotation leads for remediation.
- Game-day frequency: quarterly cross-team full-day exercise focusing on multi-service orchestration.

Grading and certification

- Passing two OSS scenarios + mentor approval => certified to respond as second-line.
- Passing three scenarios + one live low-impact incident => eligible for solo oncall.
- Certifications tracked in People Ops training profile.

Communication templates

Below are canonical, brand-safe templates for incident updates. Always: brevity, what we know/ don’t know/ next steps, impact, ETA, contact. Tailor tone to customer impact and confidentiality level.

1) Initial customer-facing status (public status page)

Title: Degraded inference latency — <region> (investigating)
Time: 2026-02-10T14:05Z
Summary: We are investigating elevated latency for inference requests in <region>. Impact: a subset of customers may see increased response times and occasional 429 errors.
What we know: Latency increase observed in the serving pool handling redwood-base-1.
What we don’t know: Root cause (investigation ongoing).
Next steps: Ops are running cache-warmup and checking autoscaling behavior. We will provide updates every 30 minutes or when the customer impact changes.
Contact: status@redwood.ai and support portal link

2) Internal bridge announcement (Slack / Bridge topic)

[INCIDENT START] 2026-02-10 14:05 UTC — Latency spike: region-nyc-1
Impact: 95th latency ↑ 220% for tenant subset T0xx. Errors: intermittent 429s.
Bridge: <link>
IC: @oncall-sre
Actions underway: cache warmup, pool scale +1, model fallback readiness.
Requested inputs: service owners for model-serving and GPU-pool.

3) Customer update (email for affected customers)

Subject: Update — Inference latency in <region> (Feb 10)
Hello,
We experienced elevated inference latency affecting some requests in <region>. Our team identified sustained cache miss rates and is executing a staged warmup and scale-up. We expect a meaningful improvement within 30 minutes. We’ll follow up with a summary once resolved. Sorry for the disruption — we know how important low latency is and we’re taking steps to prevent a recurrence.
Regards,
Redwood Inference Support Team

4) Status resolved (status page + internal)

Title: Resolved — inference latency in <region>
Time: 2026-02-10T15:12Z
Summary: The latency spike has been resolved. Root cause: cache churn on the serving pool amplified by a synthetic load pattern. Remediation: completed cache warmup and scaled pool for short window. Next steps: post-incident action items and follow-up scheduled.

Mini post-incident template (15-minute synth postmortem)

1. Incident ID: INC-YYYYMMDD-NNN
2. Timeline (HH:MM UTC): pager -> bridge -> mitigation -> resolve
3. Impact summary: which tenants, SLOs breached (if any)
4. Root cause hypothesis: short paragraph
5. Immediate remediation taken
6. Action items (owner, due date)
7. Communication summary

Runbook & checklist index (quick links)

- KV-cache cold start: oss/runbooks/kv-cache-coldstart
- Throttle/backpressure: oss/runbooks/throttle-backpressure
- Model-fallback: oss/runbooks/model-fallback-and-compatibility
- Quality-regression: oss/runbooks/quality-regression-triage

Pager criteria (table)

| Severity | Symptom examples | Page to | SLA / Time to action | Primary owner |
| P0 | Complete region outage; 100% errors | oncall-sre + eng-platform | 1 min | Eng SRE |
| P1 | SLO breaches, 95th latency > 2x baseline, customer-impacting errors | oncall-sre | 2 min | Serving Runtime |
| P2 | Increased error rate for subset of tenants; performance degradation | oncall-ops | 15 min | Platform Ops |
| P3 | Non-urgent config drift, alerts with noisy telemetry | oncall-dev | 1 business day | Service Owner |

(Use judgment; when in doubt, page the next higher severity.)

Evidence collection checklist

1. Alert IDs and timestamps.
2. Bridge link and participants.
3. Top 3 stack traces / error messages.
4. Relevant metric snapshots (PNG or dashboard links).
5. Commands executed and outputs (copy/paste).
6. Logs: correlate span IDs and request IDs.
7. Customer tickets opened/impacted tenants listed.

After-action items + prevention library

- If root cause is cache churn, add a low-latency warmup window to autoscaler runbooks.
- If model fallbacks are frequent, publish a compatibility matrix for model variants and CPU/GPU profiles.
- Track mean time to evidence (MTTEv) as metric for operator readiness; goal < 45 minutes for P1s.

Onboarding tasks for new responders

1. Read the top-5 runbooks listed above.
2. Complete two OSS shadow exercises as observer.
3. Run one supervised simulated incident and submit evidence.
4. Pass mentor signoff and complete certification survey.

Retention & continuous improvement

- Rotation leads must schedule a retro after each OSS run to capture easy wins and adjust scenarios.
- Maintain a library of anonymized incident timelines for training.

Appendix: sample automatic evidence form (fields to populate)

- Incident ID
- Start time (UTC)
- Acknowledge time (UTC)
- Initial severity
- Summary of symptoms
- Commands executed (copy/paste)
- Metric screenshots (links)
- Resolution steps
- Postmortem owner (name)

Appendix: CLI snippets and links

- List pods by label:
  kubectl get pods -l app=serving-runtime -n redwood-prod
- Check autoscaler status:
  kubectl describe hpa serving-runtime-pool -n redwood-prod
- Query cache metrics (Prometheus example):
  prometheus_query 'kv_cache_hit_ratio{tenant="T01"}'

Questions or improvements? Contact the rotation lead or send feedback to oncall-process@redwood.ai.
